translations.text: Jesus ✠ Christ. A eulogy by our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Stephen, bishop of the city of Heracleopolis, which he delivered on the feast day
of the holy martyr of Christ Jesus, Apa Elias, on the sixteenth of Phamenoth [?], as they celebrated his feast in his shrine. In peace. Amen.
There are trees in distant lands which, although we have not seen them face to face, we come to know for their beauty and sweetness by enjoying their fruit.
For prize-bearing martyrs such as these, who arose in city after city and in region after region, even if we did not go
with them to the tribunal, nor witness the contest that they endured for Christ,
yet through the great number of gifts present in their shrines we know their greatness and their honor before the Lord.
Such indeed is our chosen crown-bearer, the honored victor, Saint Elias, who is the reason for your gathering today, you devout people.
O victor Elias, radiant in both name and virtues!
I see the holy declaration of our Savior fulfilled in you: “Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.”
Now Christ said this about all the righteous.
But Saint Elias himself became like the sun in his name, his virtue, and his radiance, through the designation expressed by his name.
For the meaning of Elias, according to the Greek language, is “the sun.”
First, the name came together with his birth in the flesh.
Afterward, his [?] became evident, confirming the name.
According to the name, then, of this saint, honor [?] of this kind belongs to him, and his blessing also, as it is written in the Psalms.
But the visible sun has a limit to its light.
The light of the martyrs, however, is imperishable.
The sun sets, and then it rises again.
The victorious martyrs also set bodily through their death,
but they will come with the Lord in glory, with the [?] of their sufferings kept safe for them.
But let us turn to the subject of your gathering to commemorate him today: Saint Elias, who guided his military service well.
Elias is truly the commander of Christ the King and the physician of everyone who is sick.
Now this man was not a laborer among those who work the land, nor
did he eat his bread in the sweat of his face.
Nor did he live in poverty, so that you cannot say that the hardship of poverty compelled him to run into this arena of martyrdom.
But he is a nobleman among those of high rank.
He is rich in visible things.
He is rich in the gifts of Christ.
He is an outstanding fighter against visible enemies.
He is an outstanding conqueror of the hidden evil adversary.
He is close to the king of this world.
And he is a friend of the King of heaven and earth, Christ Jesus.
He was enlisted for military service in the earthly regiment.
He too was enrolled in the heavenly ranks through the struggle of confessing his faith.
He was also at first a physician in a single city.
But now he has become a healer of those near him and those far away.
Beautiful is the arena of your martyrdom, you who are truly noble!
Your crown is unfading.
The fruits of your righteousness are beyond counting.
To whom among the saints shall I compare you, O Saint Elijah?
I will compare you to the one who shares your name, Elijah,
who was taken up by horses and chariots of fire,
who shut heaven and opened it again by the word of his mouth.
For that Elijah was the one who fasted forty days and forty nights.
Oh, such a great miracle-worker! After he had burned the two captains of fifty and their hundred soldiers,
and after he had slaughtered the priests of Baal, numbering four hundred,
why did he flee before the threat of a prostitute?
You too, O victory-bearer, prize-bearer, God-bearer, Spirit-bearer and crown-bearer of the New Covenant,
the honored martyr.
The bold and noble man.
The undefeated athlete.
The victorious contestant.
[like] the holy Elijah, you stood firm against the threats of the kings, and you were not ashamed before the face of the potentates.
You trampled on the power of fire.
You proved strong in the battle against your enemies.
I will compare you to the wise Daniel, for you are truly like him in warfare and in virtue [?] together.
He, for his part, stood up to the kings of the Chaldeans.
And you also, O honored athlete, you did not stand firm for a single inheritance [?] with them,
He disregarded the decrees of Darius and Cyrus.
You too, crown-bearer of Christ, disregarded the idol worshipers.
They threw Daniel into the lions’ den because he did not obey the decree of the Persians and the Medes.
But you, righteous man, did not endure only the ordeal of wild beasts for confessing Christ.
but you proved strong in many contests.
We compare [him] to the wise physician, the beloved Luke the Evangelist.
You became like him in following Christ and in bearing witness to him.
I will therefore portray for you the story of Saint Elijah—or rather, the grace that came to him from the Lord.
Shall I speak of his struggle for God?
Or rather, of the help of the Most High that came to your aid?
Shall I speak of the tyrant’s anger and madness, or rather, of this holy martyr’s endurance?
He was like sheep among wolves.
He was like lilies among thorns.
He was a giver of light in the midst of those who were in the darkness of the error of idols, and those people were living in luxury.
But the noble man, for his part, was kept in check through [?] God.
Those people worshiped what their own hands had made, but Saint Elijah worshiped the Creator alone, who is God.
And the world-ruler of darkness was again urging him toward the things of darkness.
The noble martyr, for his part, had his citizenship in heaven.
Now picture the splendid theater, full of grace.
One man alone, our saint [?], standing between God
[?] people, between the angels and the demons.
Those on earth were forcing him to offer sacrifices to earthly beings.
Christ, the king of heaven, in turn strengthened his noble champion for the contest.
“Will you not sacrifice, then, Elijah?” “No,” he said.
The holy martyr said, “I am a physician, and I practice medicine on others.
How, then, could I allow my soul to become sick through idolatry?
I am a soldier in the army on earth, but I do not want to be separated from the armies of the angels.
I am a citizen of the city on earth, but from this day onward I will choose for myself the heavenly Jerusalem, the true city of the Holy One.”
What, then, will the powers of darkness do now?
What will the king who fights against God do?
He flattered.
He threatened.
He pleaded.
He grew indignant.
And, to put it briefly,
the rain came down.
The rain came upon them, [the winds] blew [?]
the winds.
They beat against the mind of this saint, but could not move him, for he was built upon the immovable rock, Christ.
then, when the first trial had ended,
they summoned the athlete and champion of truth into the contest.
Once again, exceedingly cruel sufferings.
Once again, confiscations and many instruments of torture.
Again, the [?] of [?].
[?] from strength to strength.
From a kingdom to another people.
From one judgment seat to another.
From many sufferings into great afflictions.
For the weapons of his warfare are not earthly, but are powers of God.
He showed himself to be following Christ, who stood before the high priest, Herod, and Pilate.
For the wise say about the nature of gold that what is tested in the furnace the first time, the second and the third is the approved gold.
As for the holy martyr Saint Elijah, he had distinguished himself in the first contest, the second, and the third.
Therefore his crown has become splendid in the heavens and on earth.
He passed through fire and water, but the resting places spoken of by the psalmist are reserved for him.
They hung him on a wooden cross, but it is enough for the disciple to become like his teacher, who was crucified for us.
He renounced his banquets of pleasure [?] and destructive enjoyment.
But the banquet of the kingdom of heaven is prepared for him.
He left behind these temporary honors, but endless blessings belong to him.
He turned his face away from the kings of the earth.
But the vision of the light of the holy Trinity, one in essence, is his.
They cut off his head with the sword, but he went to his true head, Christ. He renounced the king’s armor and became like David, who threw off Saul’s armor.
Women came out to meet that man, dancing to celebrate his victory over the Philistine.
But for this courageous man, angels are the ones who award him the prize, because he has conquered the father of all the Philistines, namely the devil.
You are blessed now, O prize-bearer, and your crown is splendid.
How splendid is your victory, O you who went through many struggles because of your love for God!
And the Lord will crown you with the crown of righteousness.
So let no one now be unbelieving when hearing of all the sufferings that this victorious martyr endured for Christ.
For the healings that take place [?] at his shrine are very numerous.
For these things spread over everyone, almost like the shining rays of the sun.
What, then, is the healing of those who suffer?
The casting out of demons.
Those who have approached the gates of death—people like these he brings back to life again through the intercessions he makes for us before the Lord Jesus.
For he knows how to heal those suffering from dropsy through his medical skill, without payment.
He knows how to heal those who suffer, removing the pain in their limbs.
In short, this holy one heals everyone, having received grace before God, giving each person what he asks of him.
Fulfilling the request of each person who comes to his holy martyr's shrine.
You see that we have a living protector, fighting for us against [?] hidden enemies.
And he also heals our bodies.
For the day of his departure, too, is fitting for this weighty subject.
For wise physicians say about this month, Pharmouthi, that it is a month that naturally produces illness.
Because it is during this month that the trees bud.
For God went down to Egypt at that time to bring the children of Israel out from among them through signs and wonders.
Also, during this month the alternation of day and night takes place with the two equal to each other.
Therefore grace has fittingly arranged that the day of this wise physician should fall on the [?] of the month [?].
so that his holy prayers may be with everyone who is sick in soul and body.
These things I have set before you, beloved, concerning the struggle of this noble martyr, Saint Elijah.
Now, my beloved, I wish to speak a solemn word concerning the holy brothers whose bones have come to his shrine.
For what is good, or what is pleasant, but for brothers to be in one place, according to the word of the hymnist David,
Again, the wise Solomon said, “There are three that walk well.”
For this reason the Lord fittingly arranged matters in this way, so that the bones of these three saints would rest beside one another.
So that the Holy Trinity, for whom they struggled, might be glorified in the naming of these three saints.
Now then, you devout people, children of grace, who wish to run well and benefit the kingdom of Christ, show diligence in coming to this place today and every day.
But do not let anyone seek only the healing of his body while we neglect the sins of our souls.
Look at the sufferings the martyrs endured, crowded into prisons, lying naked, their blood flowing onto the ground, hungry and thirsty, their bodies covered with wounds, because they did not give up.
praising God by night and by day.
Oh, what a great disgrace! We sleep with our bellies stretched out, paying no attention to the sufferings the saints endured until they became worthy of life.

Especially Jesus, the Lord of the saints, who spent the night keeping watch in prayer, not for his own sake—certainly not!—but for our sake, wretched as we are, so that he might teach us the way to escape the snares of the evil one.
See how empty everything in this world is!
What do we gain by celebrating the feasts of the martyrs who struggled against sin to the point of death because of their faith in the Son of God?
Yet we ourselves are full of passions of every kind and sins in many forms, and we have not repented before the examiner comes for us.
A little more time [?] ... [?] and the face [?], and test his mercy, of what kind it is [?].
He may find that it has no kernel inside—that is, deeds full of every virtue—but is merely in the form of husks. This is hypocrisy.
The name we bear and our rank are one thing, while the deeds we do in secret are another.
As it is written: “The things they do in secret are shameful even to speak about.”
Woe to the person who makes room for Satan to dwell within him through the desire for impurity, for he has not let him find rest while he is alive.
And if he dies before he repents, he will remain in that place forever; he will not find [?] ... he did not seek [?] ...
For [he?] said [?] that there were some among his disciples who would say it in order to preach.
Luke the evangelist said, “He gave them authority to cast out unclean spirits and to heal every disease and every sickness.”
Whoever casts the unclean spirits out of himself—that is, impure thoughts—heals his soul and his body.
O human being, cast these passions out of your soul—that is, greed—and you will be saved from the sleepless worm in Hades.
Drive away from yourself the desire of the flesh that fights against the spirit, and you will not be thrown out of the heavenly dwellings.
Do not let our honoring of the martyrs consist only in entering their shrine.
But let us imitate their courage; let us hold fast
to their endurance.
Let us be zealous for their love toward God. Those men
conquered the world and its desires of every kind. As for us,
let us not let the world and its will conquer us. Those men
despised the threat of the tortures. As for us, let us not be conquered through the deceit [?] of the devil.
They gained for themselves fellowship with those in heaven.
But let us, for our part, establish our citizenship in that place.
For this is the way we will become companions and brothers of the saints.
And if we are not in a martyrdom like Saint Elias, then
let us live in righteousness like the brothers who are beside him.

This other thing too belongs to the wisdom of God: he arranged that the bones of these ascetics should lie beside those of the martyr, so that their example might become an encouragement for everyone toward repentance [?].
Then again, if you are in a time of persecutions, here is the one who conquered in the persecutions: Saint Elias. And again,
if you are without persecution, here are those who proved themselves approved in conduct and asceticism. For
the life of asceticism is of equal worth, not falling short of martyrdom. And
to show that this is so, I will bring you the wise apostle as advocate for this argument.
when he recounted to us the faith of each of the saints.
And when he had come to the midst of Gideon, Barak, Samson, David,
and Samuel, having listed those who conquered in the stadium of martyrdom, he joined to them the life of monasticism, saying thus:
“They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the ground, needy, oppressed, and suffering—people of whom the world was not worthy.”
Finally, he crowned them all with the name of martyrdom, saying, “Therefore, since we have this multitude of witnesses set before us, let us run with endurance the race set before us.”
You see that the monastic life is the sister of martyrdom for anyone who practices it without hypocrisy or a cloak of lies.
For Christ himself gave us a model of these two struggles in his own person.
For he defeated the devil when he withdrew into the wilderness.
Again, he also established the salvation of the whole inhabited world through the victory of the cross. To those in the deserts
he gave the crown by becoming their leader in this. Again,
to those who gave themselves to the stadium of martyrdom he became a crown.
As for us, my brothers, let us follow the Lord and the things of the Lord. Let us confess
the Lord and the holy martyrs.
Let us be holy for him, like those who purified themselves for him through asceticism. Let us keep watch
over our faith like the holy martyrs.
Let us share in the love of the Spirit.
For even if we will not shine like the sun, let us at least be seen among the stars.
This is what I say: even if we cannot attain to the greatness of the contests of the martyrs, yet
let us at least be found in the [?] (rank?) of the faithful. Even
if we cannot love God as he loved us, yet let us love one another in our own way
And even if we have nothing to give him, comfort him with your words; strengthen him with the promise of the kingdom of heaven.
Say of him, as is fitting, with the apostle: “The sufferings of this present time are not worthy of the glory that will be revealed to us.”
For poverty is a martyrdom for anyone who bears it with thanksgiving.
For this is what Christ, the life of us all, said: “Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.”
And those who have been persecuted for righteousness—they are the ones who will be called children of God—are the martyrs.
As for us, my beloved, let us love our neighbors as the martyrs loved God and poured out their blood for him, so that we may find mercy on the day when we run to him.
May the Lord bless you all, from the least to the greatest, and rouse you from this negligence.
and be sober and watchful, for your adversary the devil walks in the darkness of night and day, and we do not see him, as he seeks to devour our souls. I exhort
all of you, each one, to examine his life, to see what he has done or what he still lacks. If
indeed he has sinned, let him repent of what he has done; and I trust in God and in the prayers of the holy martyr Saint Elias that he will forgive him.
Let us not put things off from day to day, so that the messenger of death overtakes us and finds us unprepared, without having repented, and we curse the day on which we were born, in vain.
For time has slipped from our hands, and the boat has been pulled ashore. Whatever is found inside it, whether good or bad, is what he has brought.
It has passed. It is good for us to repent before the door of repentance is shut against us.
May our God, Christ Jesus, the Lord of heaven and earth, place his peace upon us and drive the devil and his demons away from us.
To him belong glory, honor, and worship, together with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, the perfect Trinity in unity and the unity in a Trinity of one substance, forever and ever. Amen.
Jesus ✠ Christ. This is the martyrdom of the holy martyr of Christ, Apa Elijah.
He completed his honored struggle, together with those who were with him [?], on the sixteenth of Phamenoth, in peace. Amen.
Now it happened that when the apostles completed their preaching according to the command of our Savior Jesus, they brought the church to completion from the places where the sun rises
to the places where it sets, so that the sweet fragrance of their offering spread [?] to the heavens, while their hearts were directed toward faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
And the name of God was glorified, and Mastema was put to shame.
The glory of the church was revealed, and the idols came to an end, until two hundred and forty-six years had elapsed since the ascension of our Savior Jesus Christ the Lord.
while the whole world was of one faith, worshipping one God, Jesus Christ, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen. Now it happened
after this, for a long [?] a long time, in which the world did not sin by worshipping idols,
And when Mastema realized that he and those who belonged to him had been put to shame,
he spoke with those who were his, saying: "What shall we do? A little more and [?] the world will not turn back to me again, and they will not listen to me." He thought
of a turning of this kind, so that he might make the world turn aside as at first. Likewise it is necessary for the martyrs to receive crowns.
He made a plan in his heart, saying, “I will enter the hearts of the great kings who rule the world and change their hearts.
I will make them abandon the God of heaven, worship idols, shed blood, and [?] engage in deeds that cause trouble for no reason.”
Now these are the names of the kings who held power at that time,
each in his own country: first, Liberianus, who ruled Konoia [?]; second, Nicomedes, who ruled Persia; third, Eutychodorus,
who ruled Media; Diocletian, who ruled the Romans; and Herodian, who ruled India.
When the devil deceived them, they abandoned the God of heaven and worshiped idols. They shed the blood of all the Christians, each in his own country.
Now there was a man named Soterichus, who served as Caesar under Herodian, the king of India.
When he saw that all the Christians were being abused because of the holy name of our Lord Jesus Christ,
and saw the great miracles that had taken place through them, he too renounced the idols and believed in the true God, Christ Jesus.
Then Saint Soterichus began to oppose the king.
He sent orders with sovereign authority and released all the Christians who were imprisoned.
When King Herodian heard this, he became extremely angry. He immediately sent orders to have Soterichus brought to him.
And when he came, the king said to him: "Soterichos, what is this audacity that you have committed in my kingdom?
You have opposed my command [?] concerning those who worship the gods, although after me you are the first in my kingdom."
Soterichus answered, “May I never again submit to a king of this world! Instead, I will serve the true king, Christ Jesus, whose kingdom neither passes away nor comes to an end.
"Now then, O king, do not trouble me. I will not worship your abominable gods, nor will I forsake my King Jesus."
When he said these things, the king became extremely angry and ordered him to be bound.
When his soldiers saw him bound, they cried out, “Our lord, give the order, and we will untie you and rescue you from the king’s hands!”
They said to them, “No, because it is the will of my Lord Jesus that I should die for his holy name.
Our Lord Jesus did not desire war, but peace.
"As for me, what I ask of you is this: that you all give me your whole heart and die for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may be enlisted [?] in the army of the angels."
They all cried out, “We are ready to do what you have said with joy!”
On that day, five commanders of a thousand were under his command, together with their large force of soldiers.
They came to the king with one mind, saying, “We are all Christians. We too will die the death that our lord Soterichus is going to die.”
When the king heard them, he became extremely angry—or rather, he was thrown into turmoil.
He ordered them to be put aboard boats and taken out to the open sea. They cut off their heads and threw their bodies into the sea, while Saint Soterichus stood over them, praying.
He looked and saw their souls going up to heaven like white doves.

And he for his part stretched out his neck, and they took off his head. And this is the way the holy Soterichos completed his martyrdom, together with his whole household and the soldiers who were with him.
Their total number was four hundred and fifty-six, together with the other five commanders of a thousand. They all met their end on the same day, the ninth of Tobe. In peace. Amen.
Listen now, my brothers, and let me tell you that God does not forget those who trust in him, but helps them and gives them strength.
Now it happened, when the holy Soterichos had become a martyr, there was
a soldier in the palace, thirty-three years old, whose name was Elias. He was handsome in his face, mighty in his strength, and perfect in every good work.
He was a physician and was always in attendance on the king because of the cures he performed. Thus, whenever an illness afflicted the king or his nobles, he was the one who treated them.
For this reason, everyone in the palace loved him, from the least to the greatest.
Saint Elijah thought about Saint Soterichus every day.
He would ask, saying, “When I am worthy, reveal yourself to me, so that I may see your face again.
As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, I too will die the death that you died.”
When he fell asleep while thinking about these things, a voice came to him: “Elijah, Elijah!”
He said, “Here I am, Lord. Who are you who is calling me?”
Saint Elijah thought that an illness had afflicted the king and that he had sent for him to treat him.
The voice came to him a second time: "My chosen one, Elias, I am not a king as you suppose, who needs a physician to heal him. Rather, open your eyes and know who I am. I
am Jesus, the sweet fragrance of the incense of the Father. I am Jesus, the true physician, who heals every disease and cures those who are afflicted,
I am Jesus, the sweet fragrance of the true vine of the good Father.
I am Jesus, the blossom of the water of the Acherusian lake.
I am Jesus, the indissoluble bond of the ages.
I am Jesus, who helps everyone who believes in him with all their heart.”
When Saint Elijah heard these things, he raised his eyes and saw Jesus mounted upon the chariots of the cherubim.
Michael the archangel was at his right, and Saint Soterichus was at his left.
He was wearing a magnificent robe, such as no king of this world could wear.
When Saint Elijah saw these things, he bowed down before the Lord, saying, “Forgive me, my Lord, for I am a sinful man. But I know, my Lord, that you grant repentance.”
the sinner, when he turns back and repents.
So I beg you, my Lord Jesus Christ, you who forgive all sinners: forgive me too for all the sins I committed when I did not know you.
At that very moment Jesus raised him up, saying to him, “Get up, my chosen one, Elijah. I
I am Jesus, who helps you. Truly I say to you, I will grant you my kingdom; for behold, I have already written your name in the book of life.
For I know that you will endure much suffering for my name, but do not be afraid.
They will not be able to overcome you, because I am with you wherever they take you, strengthening you until you finish your struggle.
But when the king sends for you tomorrow, do not go to him according to your [?]. He will send for you a second time, and they will compel you until they bring you to him.
He will ask you, 'Why did I send for you, and you did not come to me in haste?' Answer
him yourself, without any fear, with the holy words that I will put into your mouth."
But I am with you, and I will fill you with the Holy Spirit, strengthening you until my name is glorified through you.
So get up now. Come and greet your companion Soterichus, whom you asked to see.”
When the Saviour had said this to him, he gave him peace and went up to heaven in glory, while the holy Elias gazed after him.
Likewise, a strong, pleasant fragrance spread through the bedroom where Saint Elijah was sleeping in the morning.
Now when it happened that the holy Elias went to the king's palace, as was his custom,
Then the king sent for him. The messengers said to him, “The king summons you, Elijah.
Why have you not come to the palace these days?”
The saint said to them, “Go and tell the king, ‘Elijah, the servant of Jesus Christ, says: From this moment on, I will not submit to you, because it is not right for the living to
submit to the dead. Rather, the dead person submits to the living one, so that he too may live through him.’”
When the messengers heard these things from Saint Elijah, they reported these words to the king.
When the king heard these things, he became very angry and sent a military commander after him to have him brought to him against his will.
and when they brought him to him, he saw that his face was very full of glory.

The king said to him, "Elias, I love you very much. Why have you become so very proud like this? You have despised me. You did not come to me, so that I had to send for you; instead you have compared me to a dead man."
Saint Elijah said to him, “All the gods of the nations are silver and gold.

They are works of human hands. Their eyes do not see; their ears do not hear; their hands do not feel; their feet do not walk. Those who made them will become like them, and so will everyone who worships them.
So look, king, you have realized that you are a murderer, insofar as you worship dead gods.
As for me, my God is Jesus Christ. He is a living God, and everyone who lives and believes in him will live in him. It is written:
In this way: “Just as my Father is alive, I too am alive because of my Father. You too will live because of me.”
When the king heard these things, he said, “Elijah, listen to me and worship my gods, so that you may escape great and terrible tortures.”
“Do you want to die the bitter death of Soterichus?”
The saint said to him, “O king, the death of Soterichus is not a bitter death; rather, it is exceedingly honorable,
because it is written as follows: ‘The death of the Lord’s holy one is precious in his sight.’”
The king said to him, “Dear Elijah, do not make me hate you for no reason.”
But Saint Elijah began to put the king’s gods to shame.
He said, “O king, since you have put so much pressure on me, I do not wish to upset you either.
But I want you to let no one enter the temple until I have finished offering a sacrifice to your gods.”
The king ordered that Saint Elijah be allowed to go inside.
Then the saint took an axe with him under his clothes.
When he saw the idols standing on their pedestals, he rushed at them with great divine power.
He threw them down from their bases, and they fell; and with the axe that was in his hand he cut their heads off their bodies.
The angel of the Lord suspended their bodies in the air in the middle of the temple.
Their heads lay at the foot of their pedestals.
Saint Elijah came outside and said to the king, “O king, show me your gods.
For I went into the temple and did not find the gods there to worship them,
since it is written in the Gospel: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him alone.’”
When the king heard these things, he quickly got up and went into the temple. He saw nothing but the heads lying at the foot of their pedestals.
He ordered the priests to be brought to him and asked them, “Where are the gods we worship?”
They were afraid and could not find anything to say. Instead, they wanted to deceive the king.
They said to the king, “O king, our lord, live forever! Our gods have fled from us,
saying, ‘Some enemies of the king want to rise against him. We will go and fight the war, and then return to you.’”
When Saint Elijah heard these things, he was very glad and laughed, saying, “So your gods forgot to take their heads with them when they went off to war!”
And when the king heard these things, he was very ashamed, but even more he became very angry. Now there was a priest [?]
He said, “You who deserve to perish by the sword! Do gods go to war without heads on them?”
While the king was saying this, a voice came out of the body of an idol suspended in the air in the temple, saying, “King Herodian, do not believe these priests
... who deceived you [?], saying, "We went to war so that we might save you."
We are not gods capable of waging war.
For behold, we were going up into the midst of [?] by the God of the holy Elias, and we were not able to save you [?], so how could we save you as well?
We beg you, O king, to ask the holy Elias not to throw us down, so that we do not become [?] fallen.
The king turned to Saint Elijah and said to him, “Elijah, I know that nothing is impossible for you, and that while you are in the palace you cure every illness without difficulty.
In the same way, I ask you to heal the gods, not to leave them suspended, and to make their heads attach to their bodies again.”
Saint Elijah said to the king, “Do humans heal gods, or do gods heal humans?”
The king said to him, “Truly, God heals humans.”
The holy Elias said, "Truly you have judged rightly, O king."
Why, then, do you compel me, saying, ‘Heal your gods for me,’ when you say that they are gods?
If they are gods, let them heal themselves.
But since you have asked me, O king, to let them down and stop them from hanging in the air, I will not disappoint you.”
Saint Elijah raised his eyes to heaven and prayed,
saying, “Hear me, Jesus, the ear that hears, the eye that sees.”
I beg you to make the idols fall to the ground, and [?], and let the memory of them perish from the earth.
Immediately the idols fell to the ground and were crushed, becoming like dust, along with their heads that lay on the ground.
Afterward a strong wind blew and scattered the dust of the idols, and they vanished from the face of the earth.
When the king saw what had happened, he said to the saint, “Elijah, is this the favor you have done me? I asked you for a favor, but you have made my gods like dust before the wind!”
The saint said to the king, “It is written, ‘The ungodly person is like dust that the wind scatters from the face of the earth.’
And you too, O king, if you remain impious, you will go to destruction like them.
When the king heard these things, he became extremely angry.
He ordered him to be locked up until the next day.
But Saint Elijah spent the whole night praying to God.
While the king was still sleeping that night, the devil came in to him in the shape of a great black dragon, with [?] on him, looking utterly terrifying.
When the king saw him, he was troubled and cried out, "Who are you, in this form, O you whom I see in this shape and this fearful appearance?"
The dragon answered, “I am the devil, the enemy of the Christians.”

“Why did you let Elijah, this Christian magician, destroy your gods? Do you want to become a Christian yourself and become my enemy? If so, I will punish you severely. For look—you can see how terrifying I am!”
The king was greatly troubled, for the eyes of the dragon were flames of fire.
The king said to him, "My lord, whatever you tell me, I will do; only do not destroy me." The devil said:
to him, “If you will obey me, when you get up early tomorrow, have gods made for you out of gold in place of these stone ones that Elijah destroyed.”
“And compel him to worship them too. If he refuses to obey you, torture him all the more.”
When the dragon had said these things, he led the king's heart astray, and he became a flame of fire and flew away.
When the king got up early, he ordered gods to be made for him out of gold in place of the stone ones, just as the devil had said.
And he had Saint Elijah brought to him.

The king said to him, “What will you say to me now? Can you still say that these are not gods? Look, I have made them out of gold. Now obey me: come and worship them before I torture you. Otherwise, I will not spare you even one more day.”
But Saint Elijah said to the king, “Whatever you want to do, do it to me quickly,
because I will not abandon my Lord Jesus Christ and worship things made by human hands.”
When the king heard this, he became very angry. He ordered them to split open his toes and pull out their bones.
The king said to him, “Elijah, you have seen the beginning of the tortures and how terrible they are. So obey me and escape this terrible torture.”
The saint said to him, “I do not care about your tortures, you son of the devil!”
When the king heard this, he became very angry. He ordered them to pull out his nails one by one, those on his hands and those on his feet.
The king said to him, “Obey me so that you can escape terrible tortures. Offer sacrifice, and I will release you.”
Saint Elijah said, “You have now done me a good turn, O king.
For it is written thus: "O death, where is your sting? The sting of death is sin." Therefore this is the sting of death, which you have plucked out of [the] heart [?].
When the king realized that he had not been overcome by this torture either,
he ordered them to strip the skin from his lips and pull out his sinews one by one.
These are the tortures they inflicted on him that day.
The king said, “Elias, there is just one more torture I will inflict on you if you do not offer sacrifice. By the well-being of my kingdom, I will put you to a terrible death.”
The holy Elias said to him, "It is written: 'Do not fear those who will kill your body; but your soul they have no power to destroy.'" These
words, when the king heard them, he ordered that he be laid on a bed of bronze and that fire be burned under him for three hours, with the fire blazing beneath him.
And they were pouring [?] over his body, but he did not feel these harsh tortures. But

He recited this psalm, saying: “The holy ones will boast in the glory of their honor; they will rejoice on their beds. The praises of God are in their throats, and double-edged swords are in their hands.”
When the king saw that he felt nothing from this torture either,
the king immediately rose from the judgment seat and went to the sea.
He had Saint Elias brought to him, along with two other very fierce beasts: a tiger
and a nursing lioness. The king ordered them to bring him a small boat with a mast. He had all its equipment removed and had Saint Elias put aboard it with the beasts.

He had it taken out into the middle of the open sea, with him tied at the foot of the mast. They cut the boat’s ropes and left it to be battered by the weather in the middle of the open sea, with Saint Elias and the beasts aboard.
He turned his face toward the east and prayed like this, saying, “I beg you, Jesus, Son of the living God, you who saved Daniel from the mouths of the lions:
save me too from these wild beasts.
You are the one who saved the prophet Jonah while he was inside the sea monster.
Save me too in the midst of this fierce open sea.”
While Saint Elias was still praying, he saw that the beasts too had turned their faces toward the east and were crying out to God in their own language.
The righteous man turned again and prayed, saying, “You who guided Joseph, guide me too, together with these two unreasoning
animals, in the midst of these waves. For just as they have cast me adrift, they have cast them adrift too. And look, they are giving glory to your holy name.”
At that very moment Michael and Gabriel came down from heaven. They went to him, greeted him, and said to him, “Be strong, Saint Elias! No one will be able to harm you.
For we have been sent to you to steer your boat until we bring you to the region of Kounthia, because a great struggle awaits you there.”
While the angels were speaking with him, one was sitting at the front of the boat
and the other at its rear. Immediately they reached the borders of Kounthia.
The angels of the Lord greeted him and went up to heaven in glory, in the peace of God. Amen.
This is the first martyrdom of Saint Elias, which he endured under Herodian, the king of India. In peace. Amen.
Liberianus, the king of Kounthia, went out to the sea. He looked out over it and saw the little boat tossing on the sea.
With Saint Elijah mounted on it and the wild beasts licking his feet, the king immediately gave an order.
that they bring him in to the shore.
He saw Saint Elijah with his face beaming with joy. The king said to him, “What country do you belong to? Where are you from?”
The saint said to him, “I am from Thentike, and I belong to Jesus Christ.”
When King Liberianus heard the name of Jesus, he stopped short, for he himself worshiped idols.
He said, “You really are one of those Christian sorcerers!
Well, look! The signs of your sorcery expose you. If you were not a sorcerer, you would not have been rescued from these fierce beasts.
But I will torture you as your sorcery deserves.”

The devil had goaded his heart into inflicting great evils on the saint. The king ordered him to be bound with iron chains and thrown into a bronze cage until the next day, when he would question him.
He also had the wild beasts taken to his menagerie.
Early the next morning, the king ordered Saint Elijah to be brought to him in the city's theater so that he could question him publicly.
When the king [?] him, the king first asked him, “What is your name?” The saint said to him, “My name in this world is Elijah, but my name in the Spirit is ‘The one called by Jesus Christ.’”
The king said to him, “So you have two names, unlike everyone else?”
The saint said to him, “I am not the only one who has two names. Rather, all who believe in my God have their strength changed,

and they receive their name according to the Spirit. For those born of the flesh are flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. Therefore, the name according to the flesh is one thing, and the name according to the Spirit is another.”
When the king heard this, he said, “Elijah, these words will do you no good at all. You will die a terrible death,
and no one will be able to rescue you from my hands.”
Saint Elijah said to him, “I would rather die at your hands
than disobey Jesus my God.”
When the king heard these things,

he ordered them to scrape his sides and the soles of his feet with iron rods. While they were scraping him, the king shouted to him, “Obey me and offer sacrifice, so that you may be spared great torments!”
But the saint did not speak at all. Instead, he kept looking up to heaven.
When the king saw that he felt nothing, he ordered them to throw him into a cauldron full of boiling oil and keep a fire burning beneath it for two hours,
so that his body would be thoroughly scorched. Afterward, they poured resin and pitch over him,
and their flames rose seven cubits above his body.
The king thought that he had already died.
Then he cried out, “Elijah, where is Jesus your God now? Let him rescue you from my hands!”
But the saint was filled with the Holy Spirit. As he was being brought into the fire, he cried out, saying, “Shut your mouth and be silent,
you lawless king, uttering the name of my God with your filthy mouth!” When the king heard that he had not died, he was utterly amazed
and clapped his hands together.
He said, “Now I truly know what I will do to you until I undo your magic. I will send for a magician more accomplished than you, and he will undo your magic.
And I will punish you.” He had him thrown into a chamber [?], suspended by his feet, and lowered headfirst into a jar full
of salt and lime, with the lime reaching his elbows. He sealed the door with his signet until he could send for the magician, bring him, and put him to the test against him.
When the king went outside the place into which Saint Elijah had been [?] brought,
Michael the archangel came to Saint Elijah and lowered him from where he was hanging. He made the sign of the seal over his body, and he became as though nothing had touched him at all.
He also brought him some fruit from the trees of paradise to eat.
For he had not eaten since the day they put him out to sea with the wild beasts.
Michael said to him, “Be strong, Saint Elijah, victorious wrestler, crown-winning master of the contest, fellow heir with Jesus Christ.
Truly I tell you, they have finished preparing your
throne in the seventh heaven, at Christ’s right hand. Do not be afraid. I will remain with you, helping you everywhere they take you.”
When the angel of the Lord had said these things to him, he went up to heaven in glory.
The king sent for a great master magician named Theocletus, who was renowned throughout the whole region of Kounthia. When he came to him,
the king said to him, “Theocletus, I have heard of your reputation as a master magician.
Now, then, let your skill be demonstrated on this Christian.
For I have heard that they have a god called Jesus. Whenever they call on his name, he helps them in every distress.”
When Theocletus the magician heard this, he laughed and said to the king, “Do not let him trouble you with these words. I will show you that I have the power to undo the Christians’ magic.”
The magician got up and [?] the king outside the palace.
They went into a tomb.
He turned his face toward the west.
He called upon the ruler of Tartarus, saying, “Send me a soul so that it may tell the king that I am capable of undoing the Christians’ magic.”
Immediately the ruler of Tartarus came up with a multitude of souls who were bound and being tortured. The magician asked the ruler of Tartarus to open the mouth of one soul so that it could speak.

When the soul was allowed to speak, it cried out, saying, “Woe to you, King Liberianus! Woe to everyone who denies this name, Jesus! And you, Theocletus the magician, you do not have the power to contend with Elias the Christian.
Yet blessed are you, because you will be saved through him, and you will receive what your name means: ‘The one whom God has saved.’
You will try to harm Elias, but he will do good to you. You will try to kill him, but he will give you life. But I implore you by the grace that will come upon you:
when you receive life through Saint Elias, remember me too before him.

Perhaps he will plead with his God Jesus, and he will relieve us in the punishments we are suffering. For we are being tormented all the more because we denied him in our ignorance while we were in the world.
Now we have realized that Jesus is a merciful God. He forgives the sins of everyone who turns to him with an upright heart.”
When the king heard these words, he said, “What are you going to do to Elias the Christian, who made the demons appear as an illusion and speak these
lying words so that we would be afraid and spare him?” The magician answered the king, saying, “Do not think that the words this soul spoke are lies. No!
For this soul said, ‘You do not have the power to contend with Elias the Christian, because his God defends him.’ I believe
that this statement is true, because I once heard about some ancient magicians who were Egyptians, two brothers, one named Jannes
and the other named Jambres. They opposed a man named Moses
and could not overcome him,
because his God defended him.
So now, O king, we too are going astray in our foolishness, for no one has power over anyone whom God defends.
But I do not want to upset you, O king. I will put Elias the Christian to the test three times. If I cannot overcome him, then truly no one has power over him.”
The king went into the chamber where the saint was shut up. He found the seal he had affixed intact, just as it had been.
The king was saying, “Perhaps you will find that he has already died from the torture I subjected him to.”
But when he opened the door and went inside, he smelled a strong, sweet fragrance in the room. He looked and saw Saint Elias standing in prayer, with great glory surrounding him.
When the king saw this, he was amazed, but at the same time the devils were leading his heart astray.
He ordered Saint Elias to be brought out. The magician said
to the king, “Let us take this Christian
up onto the mountain, away from these crowds, so that the two of us can test each other.”
And the king [?] went up onto the mountain with the magician and the saint.
The king said to him, “O Elias, I have brought you onto this mountain to test you today.” The saint said to him, “I do not know what magic is, but the power of Jesus my God cannot be overcome.”
The king turned to the magician and said to him, “Whatever you are going to do, do it quickly.”
The magician stood up and invoked his powers, and the mountain split in two.
Two huge, extremely fierce dragons came up. But Saint Elijah did not look at them at all; instead, he stood praying to God.
When the dragons saw Saint Elijah praying, they stopped short
and stood still. Fear would not let them attack him. When the magician saw this, he was utterly amazed. He labored at his invocations, but the dragons did not stir from their place.
The magician wanted to please the king. He said, “Elijah, do you think that you have restrained the dragons
and prevented them from attacking you because my arts have run out? Look, I tell you, I will do something worse than this to you.”
Afterward he made an invocation, and the dragons split down the middle. He took the dragons’ gall, their [?], and their liver, along with a deadly [?] and a wild gourd, and they were mixed together.
He put them into a new cup and invoked demonic names over them,
so that the abyss split open, the devil came up, and the whole mountain filled with demons and apparitions.
When the king saw this, he was very glad
and took hold of the magician’s head and kissed it, saying, “Truly, I have realized that you are capable of undoing the Christians’ magic.” The magician mixed the foul substances
together, put them into the cup, and held them out to the righteous man. When he took it, he said, “I did not wish to drink these foul substances.
Nevertheless, it does not concern me, for it is written in Scripture, ‘Even if they drink a deadly poison, it will not harm them.’” Then Saint Elijah looked up to heaven
and prayed in these words: “Hear me, my Lord Jesus Christ, you who hear everyone who calls upon you, who heard Abraham during his stay in a foreign land
and rescued Isaac from the hands of the Philistines,
who rescued Jacob from the hands of Esau, who rescued Joseph from the hand of Potiphar’s wife,
who rescued Moses from the hands of Pharaoh
and from the hands of Jannes and Jambres.
I too, your servant Elijah, beg you to rescue me from the power of these apparitions. Do not let them overpower me, so that the enemy may not boast over me.
For I have heard in the Holy Scripture, ‘If God is the one fighting for us, who can oppose us?’ And again Elisha says, ‘Those fighting for us are more numerous than those opposing us.’
"Now therefore, my Lord Jesus Christ, who saved Elisha from the hand of the king of Syria, save me too from the hand of these demons." It happened
that, when the blessed Elijah had finished pleading, Michael the archangel came to him, scourged all the demons, and drove them out of the mountain.
The devil too became a flame of fire and went away. The king, however, did not see the angel; only Saint Elijah did.
When Saint Elijah saw the angel standing beside him, he rejoiced greatly and made the sign of the cross over himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
He drank the cup full of foul substances, and no harm came to him.
But his face was cheerful, like that of someone filled with wine.
When Publianus saw that Saint Elijah had suffered no harm,
he raised his hands and cried out, saying, “Truly, there is no god in heaven or on earth like Jesus Christ, who is powerful, the God of Saint Elijah!”
The magician answered, saying, “There is just one more thing with which I will test you.
If you suffer no harm, then your God is truly real.”
Immediately the magician uttered an invocation, and a great fiery rock rose up from the mountain in front of them.
He said to the righteous man, “If you trust your God with all your heart, believing that Jesus is a powerful God, then come and go into this fiery rock.
And if you suffer no harm, then I too will believe in your God.”
Saint Elijah raised his eyes to heaven and prayed, saying, “I beg you, Jesus, for whom nothing is impossible.
I beg you, Jesus, the hope of those who trust in him. I beg you, Jesus, the boast of the righteous, the crown of the martyrs. You are the one who said in the holy Scriptures, ‘No fire will harm you.’
Again you said, ‘Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.’ I am therefore confident that you have power over everything.
You who rescued the three holy men from the blazing furnace, rescue me too, so that your glory may be revealed before this magician
and Publianus the senator.” Immediately a cloud of dew came out of heaven and covered the saint’s body like a garment.
He marked himself with the seal and went into the fire.
He spent two hours in the midst of the fire, praying. Afterward he came out of the fire.
He had suffered no harm at all, and there was not even a smell of fire on his clothes.
The magician and the senator approached him and greeted him, saying, “Truly, your God Jesus is a true God,
and nothing is impossible for him. We beg you, holy Elijah, to ask your God to grant us the crown of being Christians.”
Saint Elijah rejoiced greatly. He stretched out his hands and prayed, saying, “I beg you, my Lord Jesus Christ, the forgiving God,
forgive Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator. You said, ‘I do not desire the sinner’s death, but rather that he turn back and repent.’
Again you said, ‘I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.’
Now, therefore, I beg you to transform this fiery rock into a spring of water, so that I may baptize those you have chosen in your holy name,
and they may receive the seal of life. You said to your disciples, ‘Go out into the whole world
and baptize all nations in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.’”
And at that very moment,
The rock of fire was transformed.
It became a spring of flowing water.
And Saint Elijah baptized Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator.
And he sealed them in the name of the Father and the Son
and the Holy Spirit, for the forgiveness of their sins.
When the king saw this, he became extremely angry because the magician and the senator had believed in the Lord Jesus. He came down from that mountain.
He ordered the magician and the senator to be beheaded together.
Publianus the senator had three friends who came to visit him while he was in chains.
They said to him, “What has happened to you, our friend? Is the king holding you over money you could not find to pay? If so,
then we will give you the amount for which the king is holding you.” He said to them, “If you want to listen to me—I am your friend—do what I tell you.
I ask nothing of you except that you acknowledge the God of Saint Elijah, so that you may receive the crown that never perishes.” Immediately they cried out,
“We are ready to die for his holy name!” They all cried out to the king, “We are Christians!” Publius the senator was there with his three friends
and his troop of soldiers and the members of their households, as well as Theocletus the magician. The king ordered pits to be dug and filled with fire, and the saints to be thrown into them.
And he burned them all on a single day. This is how they completed their martyrdom: Publius the senator and
Theocletus the magician and everyone with him, numbering nine hundred and seventy-four. On the twentieth of Meshir, they went up to heaven in glory.
After this, they brought Saint Elijah before the tribunal.
The king said to him, “Elijah, do you think that because you have killed my magician, I will be afraid of you and release you?
By the power of my kingship,
I will torture you cruelly, until I see whether Jesus can rescue you from my hands!”
But Saint Elijah remained silent and did not speak at all.
Instead, he kept looking up to heaven.
The king ordered them to insert skewers:
two red-hot ones into his ears, and two more into his eyes.
After that, they were to pull out his tongue,
so that his brain would be pierced. After that, he ordered them to place him on a bed.
in this furnace, and pour boiling lead down on him.
But Saint Elijah endured this further torture with
fortitude.
Afterward, he had the skin stripped from his head and had [?] applied to him.
And the saint endured this further torture. Afterward, he ordered a pit to be dug in the ground, matching his height and width. He had the saint lowered
down into it. Afterward, he had a fire lit beneath a bronze cauldron full of lead until it became like water. They were to turn the apparatus and pour it down over his body until it reached
up to his neck. Immediately Michael the archangel stood over him. He did not let the fire or the boiling lead touch him at all; instead, it was like cold water around him.
When the king saw that it was not affecting him, he became extremely angry.
The king stood up and took his sword himself. With his own hand he slit open the righteous man's belly, and his intestines fell down onto the ground.
Immediately, a cloud of light overshadowed him. The angel of the Lord picked up his intestines and put them back inside his belly as before,
and stroked his whole body. He became as though they had not touched him at all.
But when the king saw that he could not overpower him,

he said, “I know what I will do. I will send him to Eutychodorus. Perhaps he has a very powerful magician with him.” He rose from the judgment seat there and ordered him to be confined until he had written his report.
He took a sheet of papyrus and wrote on it as follows: “I, Liberianus, king of Cunthia, write to Eutychodorus, king of the Medes. Greetings.
Since the Christians have rebelled through acts of magic and deserve death,
look, I have sent you one of them, whose name is Elijah, so that you may put him to death.”
Then he ordered Saint Elijah to be brought out and handed over to two imperial guards. They boarded a boat on the sea. As for Saint Elijah, they bound him and threw him into the ship's hold.
When they had sailed away [?], Michael came down from heaven with a cloud of light. He went down into the ship's hold, untied Saint Elijah, and lifted him onto the cloud of light.
He took him up into the heavens.
He saw all the saints and greeted them, and they encouraged him. He took him up to the third heaven
and also to Paradise, with the tree of life in its midst.
Again he took him into the land of the inheritance.
He saw it: its soil was white like fine silver, and it was full of trees laden with very fine fruit.
Again they took him to the city of Christ.
And twelve walls surrounded that city.
Again they showed him a great house like a royal palace, built inside the wall. It covered sixteen arouras, was built entirely of gold and pearls, and was a thousand cubits high.
Its roof was built of precious stones and shone more brightly than the sun.

Michael said to him, “Saint Elias, this house built of gold and pearls is yours.” When Saint Elias heard these words, he rejoiced greatly. While he was walking through the city, suddenly the Lord Jesus came out of heaven before him.
He said to him, “Be strong, Elias, my beloved. Your struggle has drawn near. Look, you have seen how many good things are prepared for those who will believe in me with all their heart.

I am Jesus, the good news of all the ages. Look, I bring good news to you too today. As for you, my beloved, when they take you to Media, Eutychodorus, the king of Media, will kill you, for you will complete your struggle at his hands.”
Saint Elias answered and said to the Savior, “My Lord, I do not want to remain among the godless nations, lest they scatter my bones and erase my memory from the earth.”

The Savior said to him, “Truly I tell you, Elias, my chosen one: just as the dew of heaven spreads over the whole earth, so my name will be glorified through you because of the miracles that will take place through your body.
And because you have asked me to have your body taken away from the nations, I will set your heart at rest and fulfill your request.
After some days I will reveal your memorial in a vision to righteous people living in Egypt. I will have them come for your body, take it up to Egypt, and lay it there.
And in the place where your body will be laid, I will have the bodies of other righteous people laid,
two of them, in it.
And the sanctuary where your body will be laid will be a temple for me forever.
And everyone who enters your sanctuary and makes any requests of me in faith in your name, I will fulfill them for him.
And all who suffer from any illness, if they enter your sanctuary and appeal to you in your name, I will grant them healing [?]. I will make your
name famous everywhere, and I will cause great miracles and wonders to take place at your tomb.”
When the Lord Jesus had said these things, [?] up to heaven in glory.
And immediately the ship docked at the harbor of Media, the metropolis of the Medes.
And the guards gave the letters to King Eutychodorus.
The second martyrdom of Saint Elias, which he underwent under Liberianus, king of Kounthia [?]. In peace. Amen.

When the report about Saint Elias was given to Eutychodorus, the king of Media, he read everything that had been written about him. He had him confined until the next day, when he would hear his case. He wrote a reply to the letters and sent them
to go to their king in their own country. The next day the king sat on the judgment seat and had Saint Elias brought before him.

The king said to him, “Elias, what are these evil things that they have written to me that you are doing? Now, then, offer sacrifice.” The righteous man answered, “It is written in the holy Scriptures, ‘You shall not worship things made by hands, for I am God, and there is no other
besides me.’” When the king heard these things, he had him hung on a ship’s mast and had arrows shot at him for three hours.
But Saint Elias marked himself with the sign of the cross.
Immediately a cloud of light covered him, and it did not allow a single arrow to touch him at all.
When the king saw this, he was utterly amazed and ordered them to take him down from the wooden frame.
The king said to him, “Elijah, I want you to explain this sign you have performed. Is it through your skill that you save yourself from these powerful arrows? I am saying to myself
that what you have done is an act of magic; otherwise you would not have survived.” Saint Elijah said to him, “O king, do not think that this is an act of magic
that I have performed. Certainly not! Rather, this is the sign of the cross of my Lord Jesus Christ.” The king said to him, “Was your Lord hung up? What did they do to him?”
The righteous man said to him, “He went up onto the cross and died for our sins.” The king said to him, “Then your God too died like every human being?” The righteous man said, “Indeed,
he is immortal, but he died and [?] rose again to give us life.” The king said to him, “Truly, I will put you too to death by the same death that your God Jesus died.”
Then he ordered them to make a cross and hang the saint on it. When they raised the saint onto it, he rejoiced because he had been found worthy of the likeness of the Lord.
Immediately, a dove of light settled on the right arm of the cross,
and another on the left arm. They spread their wings over him and covered him, because he was naked.
Then a voice reached him, saying, “O Elijah, here is the likeness that I, the Son of God, bore. Look, you too have borne it.
For they hung me on the cross and placed me between two robbers. Truly I tell you, my chosen Elijah, there is nothing greater than the likeness you have borne.”
When Jesus had finished speaking with him, there were [?] and flashes of lightning. Great fear
fell upon everyone around him.
Then the angels came, untied the saint, and took him down from the cross. They took the cross and hurried away, leaving Saint Elijah standing.
When the king saw these things, he was amazed. He rose from the judgment seat that day and had him imprisoned until the next day. The next day, the king became very angry because the devil had

filled his heart with every kind of [?] against him. Immediately he sat on the judgment seat and ordered the saint to be brought to him. The king said to him, “Elijah, do you think that because you performed
magic tricks and survived on the cross, there is no further torture for you?” The king ordered them to crush the joints of his hands and feet.
But he endured it.
He also had them strike his head with an iron [?] until his brains came out through his mouth and nose.
When the king saw that he had not died from all these things he had done to him,
he had some extremely vicious wild beasts brought to him: a leopard and a wild boar.
He had Saint Elijah thrown to them, thinking that they would tear him apart immediately.
When the beasts saw Saint Elijah praying to God, they ran up to him, wagging their tails at him. They bowed down and paid homage to him. The king,
however, was utterly amazed. Realizing that he could not overpower him, he sentenced him to be beheaded and ordered that he be taken to an island in the sea and left there.
As they were about to take Saint Elijah out to behead him, he turned his face toward the east and prayed in this way, saying, “I praise you, my Lord Jesus Christ.”
Since I have been worthy to reach this hour, to die for your holy name, I beg you, my Lord: do not put me to shame when I come before you.
Immediately the Lord’s sweet voice came to him: “Truly I tell you, my chosen Elias, my Father’s heart is satisfied with your struggle.
Look, [?] in heaven have been crowned before you. Conquer, you who have conquered! Be strong, you who have been strong!”
When Saint Elias heard these things, he made the sign of the cross over himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
He stretched out his neck, and they cut off his head at the sixth hour on the sixteenth day of Paremhat.
The angels and all the saints came out to meet him and greeted him.
They sang the song of Alleluia until they brought him to the city of Christ.
After they had cut off his head, they took his body and placed it on an island in the middle of the sea,

until the day when God revealed it in a vision to two righteous monks in the land of Egypt, so that they would go to fetch his body, bring it to Egypt, and place it in the place the Lord had prepared for him.
This is how he completed his martyrdom and went up to heaven in glory. He received the imperishable crown in peace. Amen.

All who suffered martyrdom with Saint Elias received the crown of life forever. They numbered six thousand four hundred and thirty souls. Together with Saint Elias, they entered into life. May their holy blessing be with us. Amen.
And this is how Saint Elias completed his honored struggle on the sixteenth day of Paremhat, having fallen into the hands of three kings, who were these:
Herodian, king of the Indians—and Saint Elias was a native of that country.
The second was Liberian, king of Kounthia. The third was Eutychodorus, king of Nemetos. Under him Elias completed his struggle and went up to heaven in glory and honor.
May we too obtain the good things of the kingdom of heaven through the grace
and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ. To him be glory, together with his good Father and the Holy Spirit,
the life-giving and consubstantial Spirit, now and always, forever and ever. Amen.
